You are an independent reviewer with fresh context. Critically verify an approved implementation plan BEFORE it is executed. Do not write or edit files.

Read:
- D:\video-indexing-yolo11\worklog\plans\2026-11-20-speedup-plan.md (the plan)
- D:\video-indexing-yolo11\CLAUDE.md (task brief summary, model rules, grading rules, hard rules)
- D:\video-indexing-yolo11\worklog\WORKLOG.md (state, measurements, open issues)
- Code: run.py, vidx/decode.py, vidx/model.py, vidx/aggregate.py, vidx/source.py, vidx/output.py, score.py, bench.py, tools/batch_agreement.py, tests/test_run.py

Context: YOLO11l per-second video indexing take-home. Reference = model on every frame; object present if detected in >= half of a second's frames; people = median floor. Baseline L4: 103.9 fps, inference ~98% of time. Deadline Sun 22 Nov 2026 23:55 PKT (today is Fri 20 Nov). Grader: RTX 4090, 32 threads, Python 3.11, 6 h cap, ~13 h unseen possibly damaged videos.

Check for, and report concretely (file:line where relevant):
1. Correctness risks vs the reference: does sampling preserve second boundaries / the "every second up to the last frame" rule / partial-failure semantics? Any way per-worker letterboxing, direct-tensor inference (bypassing predict()), BGR->RGB handling, NMS args, or cross-video batching could change detections relative to Ultralytics predict() defaults? Is FP16 allowed by the rules as written in CLAUDE.md?
2. Validation gaps: is tuning strictly on train-00000 with holdout only scored? Can the sampling simulator be trusted (tune dumps contain every frame's counts in decode order; check run.py dump_frames fields)? Is the margin check well defined?
3. Feasibility and ordering against the deadline; anything that should be cut, reordered, or is missing (e.g. warmup, cudnn.benchmark, spawn + CUDA, pickling overhead, Colab low core count, memory, resume/checkpoint interplay with out-of-order video completion in the pipeline, OutputWriter sidecar semantics).
4. Anything that violates CLAUDE.md hard rules.

Return a concise list: BLOCKERS (must fix before execution), IMPORTANT (should change), NITS. For each, the concrete suggested change. Under 600 words.

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

13	1. **The model is ~98% of the time** (holdout split: infer 9,617 s, decode 180 s). 14	2. **FP32 today.** `vidx/model.py:infer` passes `half=False`. The L4 and the 4090 both have FP16 tensor cores; FP16 typically gives ~2× on YOLO-L.
15	3. **Every frame goes through the model,** but the grading per second is a vote: object present if seen in ≥ half the frames, people = median (rounded down). 21	   - One video at a time leaves the GPU idle during decode and gives small last batches.

77	- **2a:** decode workers + a plain `multiprocessing` queue (letterboxed numpy arrays pickled through the queue) + cross-video batching + direct-tensor inference.

80	**Main process (GPU owner)**

83	- Feeds (video_id, bytes) to a bounded task queue.

90	- Sends small metadata messages: (video_id, second, slot, letterboxed shape); per-video end message with per-second frame counts and any error text.
91	
92	**GPU loop (main process)**
93	- Bucket frames by letterboxed shape **across videos**. Flush a bucket at batch size B, or when it is old or the queue runs dry.
94	- Copy to pinned memory, transfer uint8 to the GPU, BGR→RGB, `.half()/255`, forward, then `ultralytics.utils.ops.non_max_suppression` with the exact predictor arguments (conf 0.4, iou 0.7, classes, agnostic False, max_det 300 — confirm the cfg defaults), counting classes only (no box rescale needed).

108	- **Offline run** (no network).

113	- `load_model()` falls back to `.pt` FP16 and logs which backend it used.

```

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. 1	# Speed-up plan: sampling, FP16, parallel pipeline, scheduling (TensorRT last)
2	
3	## Context
4	The brute-force baseline is complete and validated (tune 33 videos / 9,144 s, holdout 66 videos / 17,586 s, deterministic, decoders agree, batching safe). On the L4 it runs at 103.9 frames/s, about 34.7 h for all 50 files and ~3.6 h for the 13 h test set. We now need to be much faster without failing the accuracy checks.
5	
6	User decisions:
7	- **Margin:** accept a setting only if it reaches F1 ≥ 0.98, people exact ≥ 0.92 and within ±1 ≥ 0.98 on **both** tune and holdout.
8	- **Scope:** staged work. Every stage leaves a validated, runnable version. TensorRT comes last, only if time remains.
9	
10	Deadline: Sun 22 Nov 23:55 PKT. The full 50-file run (for `results.jsonl.gz`) must also fit before then.
11	
12	## Research findings (what limits us)
13	1. **The model is ~98% of the time** (holdout split: infer 9,617 s, decode 180 s). The `infer` timer in `run.py:process_frames` also includes Ultralytics' CPU work: per-image `LetterBox` in a Python list comprehension, `np.stack`, BGR→RGB flip (`predictor.py` v8.3.100), plus `setup_source` on every `predict()` call. So part of "infer" is single-threaded CPU work, not GPU work. Stage 0 measures this.
14	2. **FP32 today.** `vidx/model.py:infer` passes `half=False`. The L4 and the 4090 both have FP16 tensor cores; FP16 typically gives ~2× on YOLO-L.
15	3. **Every frame goes through the model,** but the grading per second is a vote: object present if seen in ≥ half the frames, people = median (rounded down). A few well-chosen frames per second usually give the same vote. This is the largest win available (~30 fps video → 3–6 inferred frames/s ≈ 5–10× less model work).
16	4. **Once sampling cuts model work, decoding becomes the bottleneck.** We still have to decode every frame: H.264 can't skip frames, and we need every timestamp to know the seconds and frames per second. On the 4090 (2–3× an L4) this matters even more. Remedies:
17	   - convert only the sampled frames to BGR (`to_ndarray` / sws_scale is a large share of decode cost);
18	   - decode in **parallel worker processes** (the grader has 32 threads).
19	5. **Letterbox compatibility:** Ultralytics uses the minimal-rectangle letterbox (`auto=True`) when all images in a call share a shape and the model is `.pt` **or a dynamic engine**. So a dynamic TensorRT engine keeps reference-identical letterboxing, and a static 640×640 one would not (CLAUDE.md rule confirmed).
20	6. **Scheduling:**
21	   - One video at a time leaves the GPU idle during decode and gives small last batches.
22	   - Cross-video batching (frames grouped by letterboxed shape) keeps batches full.
23	   - Longest-videos-first ordering avoids a long single-video tail at the end of the run.
24	
25	## Process
26	- Before execution, a separate subagent with fresh context verifies this plan independently (workflow step 2).
27	- Execution is done with Sonnet, with `/code-review` after each stage.
28	- Stage 0's numbers decide which later steps are worth doing.
29	
30	## Stage 0: profile (≈30 min Colab, small code change)
31	- In `vidx/model.py:infer`, collect Ultralytics' per-result `r.speed` (preprocess / inference / postprocess ms) into the `Timers`. Write them to `--stats-json` and add them to `Timers.summary` (`run.py`).
32	- Add a decode micro-benchmark to a new `tools/profile_decode.py`: decode only, decode + full BGR conversion, decode + conversion of 1 in 6 frames, each with `thread_type` AUTO at 1/2/4 threads.
33	- Run on 5 tune videos with `bench.py run --label profile`, sampling GPU utilisation with `nvidia-smi dmon`.
34	- **Output:** the real split of CPU preprocessing / GPU / NMS / decode. This decides whether Stage 2 is needed on the L4 and how many workers to start.
35	
36	## Stage 1: sampling + FP16 (biggest gain, smallest change)
37	### 1a. Offline sampling simulator (no GPU)
38	New `tools/simulate_sampling.py`:
39	- reads the tune per-frame dumps (`$DRIVE/frames/*.npz` from step 9: `t`, `counts` for every frame);
40	- re-aggregates using only the selected frames, through `vidx.aggregate.aggregate`;
41	- scores against `ref_tune.jsonl` using `score.py`'s functions (import, don't duplicate);
42	- reports, per strategy: F1 / exact / within±1 and the fraction of frames inferred.
43	
44	Strategies:
45	- **Fixed k per second:** k = 1…8, evenly spaced (`idx_j = floor((j+0.5)·n/k)`). Also a variant that anchors the first and last frame.
46	- **Adaptive:** k0 frames first, then add frames up to k1 for a second only if the k0 frames disagree (an object's vote isn't unanimous, or the person counts differ).
47	- **Rule:** choose the cheapest strategy that meets the margin on tune with extra headroom. Use adaptive only if it is clearly cheaper than fixed k at the same accuracy.
48	
49	### 1b. Implement sampling in the pipeline
50	- New `vidx/sampling.py`, pure functions: `pick(n, k)` and adaptive-refine helpers (unit-tested).
51	- Change `vidx/decode.py`:
52	  - decode every frame and stamp it (unchanged `Timestamper`);
53	  - group raw `av.VideoFrame`s by second (`int(t)`), buffering only the current second (≤ ~60 YUV frames);
54	  - when the second closes, select indices, then convert and rotate **only** those frames;
55	  - yield them with the second's frame count `n`.
56	- Adaptive (only if chosen): buffer converted candidate frames for a chunk of ~16 seconds. Pass 1 infers every second's k0 frames in one batch; pass 2 infers the extra candidates only for seconds that need them. Batches stay large and memory stays bounded.
57	- `aggregate` stays unchanged: it votes over the sampled frames, and second numbering is still the same (every frame is timestamped).
58	- New flags `--sample K` (and `--refine K1` if adaptive), defaulting to the tuned values, with `--sample 0` meaning every frame. The grader command stays `run.py --input --output`.
59	
60	### 1c. FP16
61	- `infer(..., half=True)`, behind a `--fp32` escape flag.
62	- Measure FP16 on its own on 5 tune videos at every frame (`score.py --only-common` against `ref_tune`), so a sampling error and an FP16 error are never confused.
63	
64	### Validation gate (Stage 1)
65	- `bench.py run --label "stage1 ..." --ref tune=ref_tune.jsonl` must meet the margin and records the speed.
66	- Then a single holdout run, `--ref holdout=ref_holdout.jsonl`, scored only and not tuned on. It must meet the margin too.
67	- Also: `check_schema`, unit tests, and per-video worst cases (no video type, such as high fps or rotated, much worse than the rest).
68	
69	### Sampling edge cases
70	- If a second has n ≤ k frames, use all of them (unit-tested).
71	- Prefer odd k, so the sampled median is a real frame count and there are no vote ties.
72	
73	## Stage 2: parallel pipeline + scheduling
74	New `vidx/pipeline.py`, used when `--workers N > 0`. `--workers 0` keeps the current single-process path for tests and as a fallback.
75	
76	**Done in two steps; the Stage 0 numbers decide what is worth doing:**
77	- **2a:** decode workers + a plain `multiprocessing` queue (letterboxed numpy arrays pickled through the queue) + cross-video batching + direct-tensor inference.
78	- **2b (only if profiling shows the queue/IPC is the bottleneck):** replace the queue payload with the shared-memory ring buffer described below.
79	
80	**Main process (GPU owner)**
81	- Reads parquet rows with the existing `vidx.source.iter_rows`.
82	- Orders the videos longest-first by mp4 byte size (check the correlation with `frame_counts.csv`).
83	- Feeds (video_id, bytes) to a bounded task queue.
84	
85	**N decode worker processes**
86	- Start method is `spawn`, created before CUDA init.
87	- Default N = `max(1, os.cpu_count() - 4)`, with FFmpeg `thread_count` 2 each, so threads don't oversubscribe the cores. Test explicitly on Colab's low core count (where N may be 1–4) as well as with a forced larger N.
88	- Each worker: decode, timestamp, sample, convert, rotate, then **letterbox in the worker** using Ultralytics' own `LetterBox(640, auto=True, stride=32)`, the identical function the reference uses.
89	- 2a: puts letterboxed uint8 frames on a bounded `multiprocessing` queue (backpressure via maxsize). 2b only: writes them into slots of a shared-memory ring buffer instead (e.g. 512 × 640×640×3 ≈ 630 MB).
90	- Sends small metadata messages: (video_id, second, slot, letterboxed shape); per-video end message with per-second frame counts and any error text.
91	
92	**GPU loop (main process)**
93	- Bucket frames by letterboxed shape **across videos**. Flush a bucket at batch size B, or when it is old or the queue runs dry.
94	- Copy to pinned memory, transfer uint8 to the GPU, BGR→RGB, `.half()/255`, forward, then `ultralytics.utils.ops.non_max_suppression` with the exact predictor arguments (conf 0.4, iou 0.7, classes, agnostic False, max_det 300 — confirm the cfg defaults), counting classes only (no box rescale needed).
95	- A second thread prepares the next batch while the current one runs (double buffering).
96	- A new `infer_tensor()` in `vidx/model.py` keeps the `load_model()` / `infer()` interface for the backend swap.
97	
98	**Completion and robustness**
99	- When a video's end message has arrived and all its frames are inferred: `aggregate` → existing `OutputWriter.write_video` → sidecar → checkpoint. Resume and checkpoint code is unchanged.
100	- A worker crash (FFmpeg segfault on a damaged file) or a per-video stall timeout: lines for the frames received so far plus one error line (same semantics as now), then the worker is respawned. One bad video never stops the run.
101	- Logging every 10 videos: queue depth and GPU idle %, showing whether workers or the GPU is the bottleneck.
102	
103	### Validation gate (Stage 2)
104	- **Direct path vs `predict()`:** identical counts on 1,000 frames (extend `tools/batch_agreement.py` with `--direct`).
105	- **Stage 2 vs Stage 1 on tune:** results identical (same sampled frames). Then holdout, plus the margin check.
106	- **Damaged input:** truncated mp4 and a corrupt parquet → error lines, and the run continues.
107	- **Kill and resume:** kill mid-run, then `--resume`.
108	- **Offline run** (no network).
109	
110	## Stage 3 (only if time remains and still GPU-bound): TensorRT
111	Per the CLAUDE.md rules:
112	- `prepare.py` exports a **dynamic**, FP16 engine on the grader's GPU in the untimed prep step.
113	- `load_model()` falls back to `.pt` FP16 and logs which backend it used.
114	- Keep it only if it passes the margin on tune and holdout.
115	
116	## Timeline (PKT) and fallback
117	| When | Work |
118	|---|---|
119	| Fri 20 evening | Stage 0 + 1a simulator → choose k |
120	| **Sat 21 morning** | Start the 50-file re-download in the background (the runtime reset wiped them). Stage 1b/1c implemented, validated on tune and holdout. **This is a shippable version.** **Fully offline run test** (network disabled); if Ultralytics attempts network calls, fix the offline settings. |
121	| Sat 21 afternoon/evening | Stage 2a (+2b only if Stage 0 says so) + validation gate |
122	| **Sat 21 night, before the user sleeps** | Launch the full 50-file resumable run (checkpoints on Drive) with the best version validated by then: Stage 2 if it passed its gate, else Stage 1. At ~6–10× it is ≈ 3.5–6 h on the L4. **Tag that commit** (e.g. `results-run`); the run uses default flags only, so the submitted `run.py` defaults are exactly the configuration that produced the results. |
123	| Sun 22 | Check the run finished (`--resume` if not), `results.jsonl.gz` + check_schema, HARDWARE.md (L4 + total time), README, ai_chats, secret scan, push. **WRITEUP.md: the user writes it, no AI; budget 2–3 h.** WORKLOG and bench_log stay current throughout so the user has the facts at hand. Stage 3 only if all of that is done. |
124	
125	**Rule after the tag:** any later code change must not alter the defaults or the results. If it would, either re-run or don't merge it.
126	
127	## Files
128	- **New:** `vidx/sampling.py`, `vidx/pipeline.py`, `tools/simulate_sampling.py`, `tools/profile_decode.py`, tests `tests/test_sampling.py`, `tests/test_pipeline.py` (fake decode and infer, like `test_run.py`).
129	- **Changed:**

140	2. Colab: `bench.py run --ref tune=$DRIVE/reference/ref_tune.jsonl` → margin met and speed logged in `bench_log.csv`.
141	3. Once per stage: holdout run, `--ref holdout=$DRIVE/reference/ref_holdout.jsonl` → margin met (never used to pick parameters).

9	`python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl`
10	For every second of every video, report which of **person, car, dog, laptop, cell phone** appear and how many people are visible. Make it as **fast as possible while still passing the accuracy checks**. Frame-by-frame brute force is the reference; our job is to get near-identical results in far less time.
11	
12	**Deadline:** Sunday 22 Nov 2026, 23:55 PKT — last commit before then is graded.
13	
14	### Data
15	- FineVideo (`HuggingFaceFV/finevideo`), first 50 Parquet files (~25 GB, ~1,600 videos, ~125 h).
16	- `hf download HuggingFaceFV/finevideo --repo-type dataset --include "data/train-000[0-4]*" --local-dir finevideo`
17	- One row = one video. `mp4` column = video bytes. `json` column = metadata (not needed).
18	
19	### Model rules (must not be violated)
20	- Ultralytics **YOLO11l**, official `yolo11l.pt`, **imgsz 640**, **conf >= 0.4**.
21	- Ultralytics defaults otherwise: aspect-preserving letterbox, **class-aware NMS IoU 0.7**, **BGR** frames.
22	- If a video has a **rotation tag**, rotate frames before inference.
23	- COCO ids: person=0, car=2, dog=16, laptop=63, cell phone=67.
24	
25	### Output (JSON Lines, line order irrelevant)
26	```
27	{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:4", "second": 12, "objects": ["person", "laptop"], "people": 2}
28	{"video": "train-00003-of-01357.parquet:5", "error": "could not decode video"}
29	```
30	- `video` = parquet basename + `:` + 0-based row index.
31	- Second N = frames with timestamp in [N, N+1), timestamps counted from the **first decoded frame**.
32	- Emit every second up to and including the one holding the last frame; empty seconds → `"objects": [], "people": 0`.
33	- Object names exactly as above. Damaged video → one `error` line; if it fails partway, keep lines already written and append one error line. Never crash the whole run.
34	
35	### How it is graded (reference = model on every frame)
36	- Object present in a second if detected in **>= half** of that second's frames.
37	- People = **median** of per-frame person counts, **rounded down** at .5.
38	- Pass needs all: objects **F1 >= 0.95**; people **exact on >= 85%** of seconds; people **within ±1 on >= 95%**. Fail → speed doesn't count.
39	
40	### Grading machine
41	RTX 4090 24 GB, 32 CPU threads, 64 GB RAM, Ubuntu 22.04, **Python 3.11**, CUDA 12 driver. Fresh VM, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, optional apt-get lines from README, optional **untimed preparation command (has internet)** — use it to fetch `yolo11l.pt` and build anything GPU-specific (e.g. TensorRT engine). Timed run has **no internet**. Hard stop at 6 h. Test set ≈13 h of unseen, possibly damaged/unusual FineVideo files.
42	
43	### Deliverables (public repo)
44	`run.py` (+ modules), `requirements.txt` (exact pins), `README.md` (install/prep/run steps), `results.jsonl.gz` (all 50 files), `HARDWARE.md` (where/what ran the full run + total time), `WRITEUP.md`, `ai_chats/` (full, unedited Claude Code `.jsonl` from `~/.claude/projects/`, tokens replaced with `[REMOVED]`; web chat share links in `ai_chats/links.txt`).
45	
46	## HARD RULES
47	- **Never write, draft, rewrite or check answers in `WRITEUP.md`.** The brief requires the user's own words, without AI. Claude may only create the empty question headings if asked.
48	- **Never commit secrets.** No HF tokens in code, notebooks, or outputs. Scan before every push (`git grep -nE "hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"`).
49	- **Never commit** data, weights, or raw `results.jsonl` (only `results.jsonl.gz`). `worklog/WORKLOG.md` IS committed: keep secrets and tokens out of it.
50	- Correctness first: every speed change must be validated against a brute-force reference on a sample before it's accepted.
51	- **Tune only on `train-00000`.** `train-00024` and `train-00049` are held out: scored only, never used to choose parameters.
52	- When anything is ambiguous, **ask the user**.
53	
54	## Workflow (agreed with user)
55	1. **Plan mode first** for every non-trivial change — planning with **Opus**.
56	2. **Independent verification** of the plan by a separate subagent (fresh context) before execution.
57	3. **Execution with Sonnet** (user switches with `/model`; `opusplan` is not available).
58	4. **After every major change, run `/code-review`** and fix findings before moving on.
59	5. Log the outcome in `worklog/WORKLOG.md`. Commit only when the user asks.
60	
61	## Inference backend (TensorRT deferred)
62	- **Now:** correct baseline with plain `yolo11l.pt` on PyTorch, then batching / pipelining / sampling / FP16.
63	- **Design for a swap:** keep the model behind one small interface (e.g. `load_model()` + `infer(batch)`) so another backend can be dropped in without touching the rest of the pipeline.
64	- **TensorRT is a stretch goal**, only if benchmarks show GPU inference is the bottleneck. If added:
65	  - Never commit `.engine` files (already gitignored).
66	  - Build the engine in a separate `prepare.py` run once by the grader in the untimed prep step on their RTX 4090 (downloads `yolo11l.pt`, exports engine). Document the command in README.
67	  - `run.py` must fall back to the `.pt` model (FP16) if the engine is missing or fails to load, and log which backend it used. A TensorRT problem may cost speed, never break the run.
68	  - Use dynamic input shapes (or otherwise preserve Ultralytics' default rect/minimum-rectangle letterboxing) — fixed 640x640 padding could change detections vs. the reference.
69	  - Keep TensorRT only if it passes `score.py` against the every-frame reference.
70	
71	## Environment
72	- Local: Windows 11, Python 3.14 (dev/editing only, no GPU work here).
73	- Compute: **Google Colab Pro, L4 GPU (24 GB)**, via the VS Code Colab extension. Code reaches Colab by `git clone`/`pull` of this repo; data lives on the Colab disk (check free space before downloading 25 GB). HF token via Colab Secrets, never in files. Colab sessions can disconnect → full runs must be **resumable** (skip videos already in the output).
74	- Target runtime is Python 3.11 + CUDA 12; keep `requirements.txt` compatible with it.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)

- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey

65	def run_inference(infer_fn, images):
66	    """infer_fn(images), splitting the batch in halves on CUDA OOM. Other failures -> InferenceError."""
67	    try:
68	        return infer_fn(images)
69	    except InferenceError:
70	        raise
71	    except Exception as e:
72	        if not _is_oom(e) or len(images) == 1:
73	            raise InferenceError(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]) from e
74	        log.warning("CUDA out of memory on a batch of %d: retrying in halves", len(images))
75	        _empty_cuda_cache()
76	    mid = len(images) // 2
77	    return run_inference(infer_fn, images[:mid]) + run_inference(infer_fn, images[mid:])

80	def process_frames(frames, infer_fn, batch_size, timers, keep_details=False):
81	    """Run frames (iterator of vidx.decode.Frame) through infer_fn in batches.
82	
83	    infer_fn(list_of_images) -> list of (counts, conf). A batch is flushed when
84	    the frame shape changes so the letterbox stays per-frame minimal.
85	    Returns (records, error). On a decode failure the records of all frames
86	    decoded so far are still returned together with the error text.
87	    An inference failure raises InferenceError (see run_inference).
88	    keep_details=False stores only (t, counts) per frame to save memory.
89	    """
90	    records = []
91	    pending = []
92	    error = None
93	
94	    def flush():
95	        nonlocal pending
96	        if not pending:
97	            return
98	        batch, pending = pending, []
99	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
100	        results = run_inference(infer_fn, [f.image for f in batch])
101	        timers.infer += time.perf_counter() - t0
102	        for f, (counts, conf) in zip(batch, results):
103	            if keep_details:
104	                records.append(Record(f.t, counts, conf, f.pts, f.rotation, tuple(f.image.shape)))
105	            else:
106	                records.append(Record(f.t, counts))
107	
108	    it = iter(frames)
109	    while True:
110	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
111	        try:
112	            frame = next(it)
113	        except StopIteration:
114	            break
115	        except Exception as e:  # decode failure: keep the frames we have
116	            error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
117	            break
118	        finally:
119	            timers.decode += time.perf_counter() - t0
120	        if pending and frame.image.shape != pending[0].image.shape:
121	            flush()
122	        pending.append(frame)
123	        if len(pending) >= batch_size:
124	            flush()
125	    flush()  # frames decoded before a decode error are still valid
126	    timers.frames += len(records)
127	    return records, error

302

306	    timers = Timers()

310	    except ResumeError as e:

315	    start = time.perf_counter()
316	    stats["startup_s"] = start - _PROCESS_START
317	    seen = 0
318	    pending = []  # (video_id, message) of videos whose inference failed: written only once we know the model still works
319	
320	    def record(video_id, lines):
321	        timers.videos += 1
322	        if any("error" in ln for ln in lines):
323	            timers.errors += 1
324	        writer.write_video(video_id, lines)
325	        if ckpt:

327

329	        for video_id, message in pending:

332	
333	    try:

19	class Frame(NamedTuple):
20	    image: Any  # BGR uint8 ndarray, contiguous, rotation already applied
21	    t: Fraction  # seconds since the first decoded frame, >= 0
22	    pts: Any  # raw pts (int) or None

26	class Timestamper:
27	    """t = (pts - first_pts) * time_base as an exact Fraction, clamped to >= 0.
28	
29	    A frame without pts gets last_t + step, where step is 1/rate if the rate is
30	    known, else the median of the positive gaps seen so far, else 1/30. If pts
31	    only appear after such frames, first_pts is chosen so the first pts frame
32	    continues that estimated timeline. Every fallback and clamp is logged once
33	    per video.
34	    """
35	
36	    def __init__(self, time_base, rate=None):
37	        self.time_base = Fraction(time_base) if time_base else None
38	        self.rate = Fraction(rate) if rate else None
39	        self.first_pts = None
40	        self.last_t = None
41	        self.gaps = deque(maxlen=101)
42	        self.index = 0
43	        self.fallbacks = 0
44	        self.clamped = 0
45	
46	    def _step(self):
47	        if self.rate:
48	            return 1 / self.rate
49	        if self.gaps:
50	            return median(self.gaps)
51	        return Fraction(1, FALLBACK_FPS)
52	
53	    def stamp(self, pts):
54	        i = self.index
55	        self.index += 1
56	        if pts is not None and self.time_base is not None:
57	            if self.first_pts is None:
58	                # t of this frame: 0 for the first frame, else continue the estimated timeline
59	                start = Fraction(0) if self.last_t is None else self.last_t + self._step()
60	                self.first_pts = pts - start / self.time_base
61	            t = (pts - self.first_pts) * self.time_base
62	            if t < 0:
63	                self.clamped += 1
64	                if self.clamped == 1:
65	                    log.warning("negative timestamp clamped to 0 (frame %d)", i)
66	                t = Fraction(0)
67	        else:
68	            self.fallbacks += 1
69	            if self.fallbacks == 1:
70	                log.warning("frame %d has no usable pts: estimating timestamps", i)
71	            t = Fraction(0) if self.last_t is None else self.last_t + self._step()
72	        if self.last_t is not None and t > self.last_t:
73	            self.gaps.append(t - self.last_t)
74	        self.last_t = t
75	        return t

78	def normalize_rotation(angle):
79	    """Counter-clockwise degrees (any number) -> 0, 90, 180 or 270."""
80	    try:
81	        a = float(angle)
82	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
83	        return 0
84	    k = round(a / 90.0) % 4
85	    if abs(a - round(a / 90.0) * 90.0) > 1.0:
86	        log.warning("unusual rotation %.1f deg treated as %d", a, k * 90)
87	    return k * 90
88	
89	
90	def _is_attached_pic(stream):
91	    try:
92	        d = stream.disposition
93	        return bool(int(getattr(d, "value", d)) & ATTACHED_PIC)
94	    except Exception:
95	        return False
96	
97	
98	def pick_video_stream(container):
99	    for s in container.streams.video:
100	        if not _is_attached_pic(s):
101	            return s
102	    return None
103	
104	
105	def stream_rotation(stream):
106	    """Rotation (ccw degrees) from stream side data, else the legacy rotate tag. 0 if none."""
107	    try:
108	        sd = getattr(stream, "side_data", None)
109	        if sd:
110	            for key in ("DISPLAYMATRIX", "displaymatrix", "Display Matrix"):
111	                if key in sd and isinstance(sd[key], (int, float)):
112	                    return normalize_rotation(sd[key])
113	    except Exception:
114	        pass
115	    try:
116	        tag = stream.metadata.get("rotate")
117	        if tag not in (None, ""):
118	            return normalize_rotation(-float(tag))  # tag is clockwise degrees
119	    except Exception:
120	        pass
121	    return 0
122	
123	
124	def frame_rotation(frame, fallback):
125	    try:
126	        r = getattr(frame, "rotation", None)
127	        if r:  # PyAV >= 14: display-matrix angle, counter-clockwise
128	            return normalize_rotation(r)
129	    except Exception:
130	        pass
131	    return fallback
132	
133	
134	def rotate_image(image, ccw_degrees):
135	    import cv2
136	
137	    if ccw_degrees == 90:
138	        return cv2.rotate(image, cv2.ROTATE_90_COUNTERCLOCKWISE)
139	    if ccw_degrees == 180:
140	        return cv2.rotate(image, cv2.ROTATE_180)
141	    if ccw_degrees == 270:
142	        return cv2.rotate(image, cv2.ROTATE_90_CLOCKWISE)
143	    return image
144	
145	
146	def _open(data):
147	    import av
148	
149	    return av.open(io.BytesIO(memoryview(data)))
150	
151	
152	def decode_video(data):
153	    """Generator of Frame for the first real video stream. Raises on open/decode errors.
154	
155	    Frames yielded before an error are valid; the caller decides what to do with them.
156	    """
157	    container = _open(data)
158	    try:
159	        stream = pick_video_stream(container)
160	        if stream is None:
161	            raise ValueError("no video stream")
162	        stream.thread_type = "AUTO"
163	        rate = stream.guessed_rate or stream.average_rate
164	        stamper = Timestamper(stream.time_base, rate)
165	        base_rotation = stream_rotation(stream)
166	        for frame in container.decode(stream):
167	            t = stamper.stamp(frame.pts)
168	            rot = frame_rotation(frame, base_rotation)
169	            image = frame.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
170	            if rot:
171	                image = rotate_image(image, rot)
172	            yield Frame(image, t, frame.pts, rot)
173	    finally:
174	        container.close()
175	
176	
177	def probe_rotation(data):
178	    """(stream_rotation, first_frame_rotation, legacy_rotate_tag) for tools/find_rotated.py."""
179	    container = _open(data)
180	    try:
181	        stream = pick_video_stream(container)
182	        if stream is None:
183	            return 0, 0, None
184	        base = stream_rotation(stream)
185	        first = 0
186	        for frame in container.decode(stream):
187	            first = frame_rotation(frame, 0)
188	            break
189	        return base, first, stream.metadata.get("rotate")
190	    finally:
191	        container.close()

2	import os
3	import tempfile
4	from pathlib import Path

6	from .aggregate import COCO_IDS
7	
8	IMGSZ = 640
9	CONF = 0.4
10	IOU = 0.7
11	_INDEX = {cid: i for i, cid in enumerate(COCO_IDS)}

13	
14	def default_weights():
15	    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "yolo11l.pt"
16	
17	
18	def summarize(cls_ids, confs):
19	    """One frame's detections -> (counts[5], max_conf[5]) in OBJECTS order."""
20	    counts = [0] * len(COCO_IDS)
21	    best = [0.0] * len(COCO_IDS)
22	    for c, p in zip(cls_ids, confs):
23	        i = _INDEX.get(int(c))
24	        if i is None:
25	            continue
26	        counts[i] += 1
27	        if p > best[i]:
28	            best[i] = float(p)
29	    return counts, best

31	
32	class Model:
33	    def __init__(self, yolo, device):
34	        self.yolo = yolo
35	        self.device = device
36	
37	
38	def load_model(weights=None, device=None, offline=True):
39	    weights = Path(weights) if weights else default_weights()
40	    weights = weights.resolve()
41	    if not weights.is_file():
42	        raise FileNotFoundError(
43	            f"weights not found: {weights}. Run `python prepare.py` first (needs internet)."
44	        )
45	    if offline:
46	        os.environ.setdefault("YOLO_OFFLINE", "True")  # Ultralytics checks value.lower() == "true"
47	    os.environ.setdefault("YOLO_CONFIG_DIR", os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "yolo_config"))
48	    import torch
49	    from ultralytics import YOLO, settings
50	
51	    try:
52	        settings.update(sync=False)  # no analytics / network calls
53	    except Exception:
54	        pass
55	    if device is None:
56	        device = "cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
57	    return Model(YOLO(str(weights), task="detect"), device)
58	
59	
60	def infer(model, frames, classes=COCO_IDS):
61	    """frames: list of BGR ndarrays. Returns one (counts[5], max_conf[5]) per frame.
62	
63	    classes=None disables the class filter (counts are still reported for the 5 classes).
64	    """
65	    results = model.yolo.predict(
66	        frames, imgsz=IMGSZ, conf=CONF, iou=IOU, half=False, verbose=False,
67	        device=model.device, classes=classes, save=False,
68	    )
69	    out = []
70	    for r in results:
71	        if r.boxes is None or len(r.boxes) == 0:
72	            out.append(summarize([], []))
73	        else:
74	            d = r.boxes.data.cpu()  # one transfer: columns x1 y1 x2 y2 conf cls
75	            out.append(summarize(d[:, 5].tolist(), d[:, 4].tolist()))
76	    return out

1	"""Per-frame detections -> per-second output lines. Standard library only."""
2	from fractions import Fraction
3	
4	OBJECTS = ["person", "car", "dog", "laptop", "cell phone"]  # fixed output order
5	COCO_IDS = [0, 2, 16, 63, 67]  # same order as OBJECTS
6	PERSON = 0  # index of "person" in OBJECTS
7	
8	
9	def median_floor(values):
10	    """Median of ints, rounded down (so 1.5 -> 1)."""
11	    s = sorted(values)
12	    n = len(s)
13	    if n == 0:
14	        return 0
15	    if n % 2:
16	        return s[n // 2]
17	    return (s[n // 2 - 1] + s[n // 2]) // 2
18	
19	
20	def aggregate(frames):
21	    """frames: iterable of (t, counts) with t an exact Fraction (>= 0) and counts
22	    a 5-sequence of per-class detection counts for that frame.
23	
24	    Returns [(second, objects, people)] for every second from 0 to the last
25	    second that holds a frame. Seconds without frames give ([], 0).
26	    """
27	    by_second = {}
28	    for t, counts in frames:
29	        by_second.setdefault(int(t // 1), []).append(counts)
30	    if not by_second:
31	        return []
32	    rows = []
33	    for second in range(max(by_second) + 1):
34	        group = by_second.get(second)
35	        if not group:
36	            rows.append((second, [], 0))
37	            continue
38	        n = len(group)
39	        objects = []
40	        for i, name in enumerate(OBJECTS):
41	            hits = sum(1 for c in group if c[i] > 0)
42	            if hits * 2 >= n:
43	                objects.append(name)
44	        people = median_floor([c[PERSON] for c in group])
45	        rows.append((second, objects, people))
46	    return rows
47	
48	
49	def make_lines(video_id, rows):
50	    return [{"video": video_id, "second": s, "objects": o, "people": p} for s, o, p in rows]
51	
52	
53	def error_line(video_id, message):
54	    return {"video": video_id, "error": str(message)}

65	def run_inference(infer_fn, images):
66	    """infer_fn(images), splitting the batch in halves on CUDA OOM. Other failures -> InferenceError."""
67	    try:
68	        return infer_fn(images)
69	    except InferenceError:
70	        raise
71	    except Exception as e:
72	        if not _is_oom(e) or len(images) == 1:
73	            raise InferenceError(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]) from e
74	        log.warning("CUDA out of memory on a batch of %d: retrying in halves", len(images))
75	        _empty_cuda_cache()
76	    mid = len(images) // 2
77	    return run_inference(infer_fn, images[:mid]) + run_inference(infer_fn, images[mid:])

80	def process_frames(frames, infer_fn, batch_size, timers, keep_details=False):
81	    """Run frames (iterator of vidx.decode.Frame) through infer_fn in batches.
82	
83	    infer_fn(list_of_images) -> list of (counts, conf). A batch is flushed when
84	    the frame shape changes so the letterbox stays per-frame minimal.
85	    Returns (records, error). On a decode failure the records of all frames
86	    decoded so far are still returned together with the error text.
87	    An inference failure raises InferenceError (see run_inference).
88	    keep_details=False stores only (t, counts) per frame to save memory.
89	    """
90	    records = []
91	    pending = []
92	    error = None
93	
94	    def flush():
95	        nonlocal pending
96	        if not pending:
97	            return
98	        batch, pending = pending, []
99	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
100	        results = run_inference(infer_fn, [f.image for f in batch])
101	        timers.infer += time.perf_counter() - t0
102	        for f, (counts, conf) in zip(batch, results):
103	            if keep_details:
104	                records.append(Record(f.t, counts, conf, f.pts, f.rotation, tuple(f.image.shape)))
105	            else:
106	                records.append(Record(f.t, counts))
107	
108	    it = iter(frames)
109	    while True:
110	        t0 = time.perf_counter()
111	        try:
112	            frame = next(it)
113	        except StopIteration:
114	            break
115	        except Exception as e:  # decode failure: keep the frames we have
116	            error = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
117	            break
118	        finally:
119	            timers.decode += time.perf_counter() - t0
120	        if pending and frame.image.shape != pending[0].image.shape:
121	            flush()
122	        pending.append(frame)
123	        if len(pending) >= batch_size:
124	            flush()
125	    flush()  # frames decoded before a decode error are still valid
126	    timers.frames += len(records)
127	    return records, error

130	def video_lines(video_id, records, error):
131	    """Records (+ optional error) -> output lines. Partial last second is kept."""
132	    lines = []
133	    if records:
134	        rows = aggregate((r.t, r.counts) for r in records)
135	        lines += make_lines(video_id, rows)
136	    if error or not records:
137	        lines.append(error_line(video_id, f"could not decode video: {error}" if error else "no frames decoded"))
138	    return lines

141	def npz_paths(directory, video_id):
142	    """(temp, final) npz paths. savez appends ".npz" unless the name already ends with it."""
143	    stem = Path(directory) / video_id.replace(":", "__")
144	    return Path(str(stem) + ".tmp.npz"), Path(str(stem) + ".npz")

147	def dump_frames(directory, video_id, records):
148	    import numpy as np
149	
150	    Path(directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
151	    tmp, final = npz_paths(directory, video_id)
152	    n = len(records)
153	    shape = np.array([r.shape for r in records], dtype=np.int32).reshape(n, -1)
154	    np.savez_compressed(
155	        tmp,
156	        t=np.array([float(r.t) for r in records], dtype=np.float64),
157	        t_num=np.array([r.t.numerator for r in records], dtype=np.int64),
158	        t_den=np.array([r.t.denominator for r in records], dtype=np.int64),
159	        pts=np.array([-1 if r.pts is None else r.pts for r in records], dtype=np.int64),
160	        shape=shape,
161	        rotation=np.array([r.rotation for r in records], dtype=np.int32),
162	        counts=np.array([r.counts for r in records], dtype=np.int32).reshape(n, 5),
163	        max_conf=np.array([r.conf for r in records], dtype=np.float32).reshape(n, 5),
164	    )
165	    os.replace(tmp, final)  # a half-written dump never has the final name

169	    """Decode + infer + aggregate one video -> output lines.
170	
171	    Raises only InferenceError (the caller must not record that video).
172	    """
173	    from vidx.decode import decode_video

178	        )

317	    seen = 0
318	    pending = []  # (video_id, message) of videos whose inference failed: written only once we know the model still works
319	
320	    def record(video_id, lines):

349	                        lines = process_video(video_id, data, infer_fn, args, timers)
350	                    except InferenceError as e:
351	                        pending.append((video_id, str(e)))
352	                        log.error("%s: inference failed, not recorded yet (%d in a row): %s",
353	                                  video_id, len(pending), e)
354	                        if len(pending) >= MAX_INFERENCE_FAILURES:  # pending ones stay unwritten: --resume retries them
355	                            print(f"aborting: {len(pending)} videos in a row failed in inference "
356	                                  f"(last: {e}). Restart the runtime and re-run with --resume.",
357	                                  file=sys.stderr)
358	                            return 3
359	                        continue
360	                    write_pending()  # the model works again, so those earlier failures were video-specific
361	                record(video_id, lines)
362	                if timers.videos % 10 == 0:
363	                    log.info("%s | %s", video_id, timers.summary(time.perf_counter() - start))
364	                if ckpt:
365	                    ckpt.maybe_snapshot(timers)
366	        write_pending()  # normal end: nothing followed them, record them as errors
367	    finally:
368	        stats["loop_s"] = time.perf_counter() - start
369	        writer.close()
370	        if ckpt:
371	            ckpt.snapshot(timers)  # also on exit 3, an exception, KeyboardInterrupt or SIGTERM; never raises
372	        print(timers.summary(time.perf_counter() - start), file=sys.stderr)
373	    return 0
374	
375	
376	if __name__ == "__main__":
377	    sys.exit(main())

1	"""PyAV decode -> (BGR ndarray, exact Fraction timestamp), rotation applied.
2	
3	av, cv2 and numpy are imported lazily so the pure helpers (Timestamper,
4	normalize_rotation) can be tested without them.
5	"""
6	import io
7	import logging
8	from collections import deque
9	from fractions import Fraction
10	from statistics import median
11	from typing import Any, NamedTuple
12	
13	log = logging.getLogger("vidx.decode")
14	
15	ATTACHED_PIC = 0x400  # AV_DISPOSITION_ATTACHED_PIC (cover art)
16	FALLBACK_FPS = 30
17	
18	
19	class Frame(NamedTuple):
20	    image: Any  # BGR uint8 ndarray, contiguous, rotation already applied
21	    t: Fraction  # seconds since the first decoded frame, >= 0
22	    pts: Any  # raw pts (int) or None
23	    rotation: int  # counter-clockwise degrees applied: 0, 90, 180 or 270
24	
25	
26	class Timestamper:
27	    """t = (pts - first_pts) * time_base as an exact Fraction, clamped to >= 0.
28	
29	    A frame without pts gets last_t + step, where step is 1/rate if the rate is
30	    known, else the median of the positive gaps seen so far, else 1/30. If pts
31	    only appear after such frames, first_pts is chosen so the first pts frame
32	    continues that estimated timeline. Every fallback and clamp is logged once
33	    per video.
34	    """
35	
36	    def __init__(self, time_base, rate=None):
37	        self.time_base = Fraction(time_base) if time_base else None
38	        self.rate = Fraction(rate) if rate else None
39	        self.first_pts = None
40	        self.last_t = None
41	        self.gaps = deque(maxlen=101)
42	        self.index = 0
43	        self.fallbacks = 0
44	        self.clamped = 0
45	
46	    def _step(self):
47	        if self.rate:
48	            return 1 / self.rate
49	        if self.gaps:
50	            return median(self.gaps)
51	        return Fraction(1, FALLBACK_FPS)
52	
53	    def stamp(self, pts):
54	        i = self.index
55	        self.index += 1
56	        if pts is not None and self.time_base is not None:
57	            if self.first_pts is None:
58	                # t of this frame: 0 for the first frame, else continue the estimated timeline
59	                start = Fraction(0) if self.last_t is None else self.last_t + self._step()
60	                self.first_pts = pts - start / self.time_base
61	            t = (pts - self.first_pts) * self.time_base
62	            if t < 0:
63	                self.clamped += 1
64	                if self.clamped == 1:
65	                    log.warning("negative timestamp clamped to 0 (frame %d)", i)
66	                t = Fraction(0)
67	        else:
68	            self.fallbacks += 1
69	            if self.fallbacks == 1:
70	                log.warning("frame %d has no usable pts: estimating timestamps", i)
71	            t = Fraction(0) if self.last_t is None else self.last_t + self._step()
72	        if self.last_t is not None and t > self.last_t:
73	            self.gaps.append(t - self.last_t)
74	        self.last_t = t
75	        return t
76	
77	
78	def normalize_rotation(angle):
79	    """Counter-clockwise degrees (any number) -> 0, 90, 180 or 270."""
80	    try:
81	        a = float(angle)
82	    except (TypeError, ValueError):
83	        return 0
84	    k = round(a / 90.0) % 4
85	    if abs(a - round(a / 90.0) * 90.0) > 1.0:
86	        log.warning("unusual rotation %.1f deg treated as %d", a, k * 90)
87	    return k * 90
88	
89	
90	def _is_attached_pic(stream):
91	    try:
92	        d = stream.disposition
93	        return bool(int(getattr(d, "value", d)) & ATTACHED_PIC)
94	    except Exception:
95	        return False
96	
97	
98	def pick_video_stream(container):
99	    for s in container.streams.video:
100	        if not _is_attached_pic(s):
101	            return s
102	    return None
103	
104	
105	def stream_rotation(stream):
106	    """Rotation (ccw degrees) from stream side data, else the legacy rotate tag. 0 if none."""
107	    try:
108	        sd = getattr(stream, "side_data", None)
109	        if sd:
110	            for key in ("DISPLAYMATRIX", "displaymatrix", "Display Matrix"):
111	                if key in sd and isinstance(sd[key], (int, float)):
112	                    return normalize_rotation(sd[key])
113	    except Exception:
114	        pass
115	    try:
116	        tag = stream.metadata.get("rotate")
117	        if tag not in (None, ""):
118	            return normalize_rotation(-float(tag))  # tag is clockwise degrees
119	    except Exception:
120	        pass
121	    return 0
122	
123	
124	def frame_rotation(frame, fallback):
125	    try:
126	        r = getattr(frame, "rotation", None)
127	        if r:  # PyAV >= 14: display-matrix angle, counter-clockwise
128	            return normalize_rotation(r)
129	    except Exception:
130	        pass
131	    return fallback
132	
133	
134	def rotate_image(image, ccw_degrees):
135	    import cv2
136	
137	    if ccw_degrees == 90:
138	        return cv2.rotate(image, cv2.ROTATE_90_COUNTERCLOCKWISE)
139	    if ccw_degrees == 180:
140	        return cv2.rotate(image, cv2.ROTATE_180)
141	    if ccw_degrees == 270:
142	        return cv2.rotate(image, cv2.ROTATE_90_CLOCKWISE)
143	    return image
144	
145	
146	def _open(data):
147	    import av
148	
149	    return av.open(io.BytesIO(memoryview(data)))
150	
151	
152	def decode_video(data):
153	    """Generator of Frame for the first real video stream. Raises on open/decode errors.
154	
155	    Frames yielded before an error are valid; the caller decides what to do with them.
156	    """
157	    container = _open(data)
158	    try:
159	        stream = pick_video_stream(container)
160	        if stream is None:
161	            raise ValueError("no video stream")
162	        stream.thread_type = "AUTO"
163	        rate = stream.guessed_rate or stream.average_rate
164	        stamper = Timestamper(stream.time_base, rate)
165	        base_rotation = stream_rotation(stream)
166	        for frame in container.decode(stream):
167	            t = stamper.stamp(frame.pts)
168	            rot = frame_rotation(frame, base_rotation)
169	            image = frame.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
170	            if rot:
171	                image = rotate_image(image, rot)
172	            yield Frame(image, t, frame.pts, rot)
173	    finally:
174	        container.close()
175	
176	
177	def probe_rotation(data):
178	    """(stream_rotation, first_frame_rotation, legacy_rotate_tag) for tools/find_rotated.py."""
179	    container = _open(data)
180	    try:
181	        stream = pick_video_stream(container)
182	        if stream is None:
183	            return 0, 0, None
184	        base = stream_rotation(stream)
185	        first = 0
186	        for frame in container.decode(stream):
187	            first = frame_rotation(frame, 0)
188	            break
189	        return base, first, stream.metadata.get("rotate")
190	    finally:
191	        container.close()
192

14	def default_weights():
15	    return Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "yolo11l.pt"

17	
18	def summarize(cls_ids, confs):
19	    """One frame's detections -> (counts[5], max_conf[5]) in OBJECTS order."""
20	    counts = [0] * len(COCO_IDS)
21	    best = [0.0] * len(COCO_IDS)
22	    for c, p in zip(cls_ids, confs):
23	        i = _INDEX.get(int(c))
24	        if i is None:
25	            continue
26	        counts[i] += 1
27	        if p > best[i]:
28	            best[i] = float(p)
29	    return counts, best

32	class Model:
33	    def __init__(self, yolo, device):
34	        self.yolo = yolo
35	        self.device = device
